summary.headline: Uniparts Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR379 crores, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin of 23.4%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the highest-revenue quarter in company history, with revenue from operations of INR379 crores (up 37% YoY, up 9% QoQ) and H1 revenue of INR726 crores (up 32%). EBITDA was INR89 crores (up 38% YoY, flat QoQ) at a 23.4% margin, and PAT rose 37% YoY to INR54 crores. Construction grew 49% YoY and small agriculture 25%, while large agriculture grew 10% against an industry decline of about 17%. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of about 24% and H2 growth slower in percentage terms than H1.

financial_highlights.change: after INR41 crores dividend paid in Q2

segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Sales grew 49% YoY; growth driven by US data-center, AI and smart-manufacturing demand and European infrastructure and energy-transition projects. Management said US growth is higher than Europe.

segments.name: Large agriculture
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10% YoY while industry volumes for tractors above 100 HP and 4WD fell about 17%. Management said the growth came entirely from new business; validation cycles run 18 to 36 months.

segments.name: Small agriculture
segments.commentary: Sales grew 25% YoY after three years of decline. Outlook: flat to up 5% in US and Canada, flat in Europe, down 15% to 20% in South America, and up 4% to 6% in India.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Share of revenue was 16.5% in Q2 vs 12.4% in Q1 FY27 and 14.7% in Q2 FY26; absolute sales grew over 50% YoY. Management flagged this segment as discretionary with expected quarter-to-quarter variability.

segments.name: Fabrication
segments.commentary: Ludhiana facility set up 2 to 3 years ago; 12% to 15% of new business wins. Management expects it to be a meaningful platform in 18 to 24 months, at high single digits to about 10% of revenue. Currently under 2% of revenue per the analyst's estimate.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to be about 24% higher than FY26.
Q3 FY27 revenue expected broadly in line with Q1 FY27, as Q3 is seasonally the lowest quarter.
H2 FY27 is expected to be better than H1 in absolute terms, but growth in percentage terms is lower because the H2 FY26 base was higher.
Management does not guide to an EBITDA figure but targets 20% EBITDA margin through the cycle.
Working capital days expected at about 135 to 140 days for FY27.
Capex of about INR60 crores over the next year, mostly approved with advances paid. Capex is about 4% of revenue.
Mexico business expected to be single-digit million dollar revenue in FY27; first customer dispatch in November 2026. Three customers in pipeline, with one started.
Medium-term growth target is mid-teens revenue growth over a cycle.
capex_capacity: Q2 FY27 capex was about INR10 crores, focused on capability enhancement, productivity and customer-led growth.
About INR60 crores of capex planned over the next year, mostly approved with advances already paid.
Restoration of the finishing shop at the Ludhiana facility is on track to be operational by end of calendar 2026.
Mexico facility to begin first customer dispatch in November 2026, to serve customers closer to their operations.
Capacity expansion at the Ludhiana fabrication facility is under way to support new OEM fabrication business.
demand_pricing: New business wins over the trailing 12 months exceed INR225 crores, mostly in construction and large ag; management defines this as estimated annual peak value, with each win reaching peak over 2 to 3 years.
Around 70% of new business awards are in construction or large ag; about 35% are in large ag.
Management said steel price increases are passed through to customers with a lag, and some material cost is yet to be recovered in Q2 pricing.
Freight costs rose in Q2 and drove higher other expenses; management expects pass-through with about a one-quarter lag.
Delivery PPM with customers is 95 plus. Management said there is no slowdown in order books and no change in delivery schedules.
Gross margin depends mainly on channel mix: warehousing sales are the highest-margin channel, followed by direct export, with local sales the lowest. Currency impact in Q2 was minimal.
Warehousing sales were 53% of revenue in Q2 vs 56% in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Europe agri demand environment, given the Ukraine-Russia war, energy prices and agri exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small ag order books are improving after three years of decline, helped by depleted inventories and replacement demand. Large ag in Europe is still muted, with recovery expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will US construction demand slow after the midterm elections or with AI capex changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the demand comes from multi-year contracts with capital committed upfront. It sees low cancellation risk, possible delays, no slowdown in its order book, and no change in delivery schedules.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise and can freight costs be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said freight was the primary driver; it is passed to customers with about one quarter lag, so recovery is expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the M&A pipeline and what is the cash deployment priority?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating about half a dozen acquisitions across hydraulics, PTO and large fabrication, after walking away from two recent deals. Acquisition is the first priority for cash, but the company will not do a deep-turnaround deal, and the Board will decide on capital allocation if no deal closes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for higher receivables, and what working capital days should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the rise to higher revenue and payment delays from one or two US OEM customers, one of which is resolved and one expected by November. Working capital days are expected at about 136 to 140.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 growth framework, and does the company expect FY27 revenue to exceed the FY23 peak in absolute terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets mid-teens growth over a cycle. It said 3PL revenue should be higher in absolute terms than the FY23 peak (INR970 crores agriculture revenue) because the company is growing faster than at that peak across all three platforms.

risks_watch: Aftermarket demand is discretionary and may vary quarter to quarter, after reaching 16.5% of revenue in Q2.
Steel price pass-through lags, so part of the material cost increase is not yet recovered in margins.
Receivables are rising due to revenue growth and payment delays at one or two US OEM customers; watch resolution expected by November.
Large ag recovery depends on new business moving through 18 to 36 month validation cycles; the industry is down about 17%.
The US FTC and USDA joint inquiry into agricultural equipment companies is unresolved; management said it sees no impact to date.
Dependence on US AI and data-center capex; management sees multi-year visibility but no order slowdown yet.
Q3 FY27 is seasonally the weakest quarter and is guided broadly in line with Q1.
Other income fell in Q2 as lower equity markets reduced treasury income.
summary.management_tone: Confident on construction, aftermarket and order visibility, with careful hedging on aftermarket variability and on acquisitions ("very, very judicious"). Management was evasive on the US FTC/USDA inquiry, declining to speculate, and it framed the receivables rise as technical customer-side issues rather than disputes.
key_quotes: Our quarter 2 FY27 has been the highest revenue quarter in the history of the company.
When market down 17%, we have grown. That growth has come entirely from new business and not from the cycle.
We don't guide to an EBITDA number, but I think the first half of this year shows the strength of our structure.
So we expect FY27 revenue to be 24% higher than FY26.

growth.why: Management reiterated (raised per brief) FY27 revenue growth of about 24% after H1 revenue up 32%, with H2 growth lower in percentage terms; backing is a >INR225 crore trailing-12-month new business win pipeline (peak value, ramping over 2-3 years) plus INR60 crore capex mostly with advances paid, though no specific capacity additions with numbers were quantified for revenue delivery.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 23.4% in Q2 and management targets 20% through the cycle, but some steel cost is not yet recovered and freight pass-through lags one quarter, so margin upside is uncertain and mainly depends on pass-through catch-up.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ludhiana finishing shop restoration is due by end of calendar 2026, Mexico first dispatch is Nov 2026, and about INR60 crores of capex over the next year is mostly approved with advances paid, though capacity was not quantified in revenue terms.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of about 24% after H1 up 32%, implying H2 growth slows, backed by over INR225 crores of trailing 12-month new business wins that ramp over 2-3 years.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management has already guided about INR60 crores of capex over the next year, but no utilisation figure was given, so a fresh capex announcement is less certain than the existing plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth was reiterated at about 24% (not raised) and H2 growth is guided lower in percentage terms than H1's 32%, with Q3 flat to Q1, so a further upgrade looks limited.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Aftermarket (16.5% of revenue, up over 50% YoY) is flagged as discretionary and variable, large ag is down about 17% industry-wide, and US OEM payment delays are lifting receivables, so H2 slippage is a real but unconfirmed risk.

rows.label: Mexico facility first customer dispatch
rows.why: First customer dispatch set for November 2026, with single-digit million dollar FY27 revenue and three customers in pipeline, one already started.

rows.label: Fabrication platform scale-up at Ludhiana
rows.why: Fabrication is under 2% of revenue today but takes 12-15% of new business wins, and management expects high single digits to about 10% of revenue in 18-24 months.

rows.label: Acquisition of hydraulics, PTO or large fabrication business
rows.why: Management is evaluating about half a dozen deals with acquisition as the first cash priority (net cash INR172 crores), but it is being very judicious and walked away from two recent deals.
